entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Second supplementary affidavit filed by the counsel for the applicant, is taken on record.

2. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Anupam Anand, learned brief holder for the State-respondent.
3.

The instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed with a prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 266 of 2024, under Sections 392, 420, 465, 411, 120B I.P.C.,
Police Station Nai Mandi, District Muzaffar Nagar, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Police Station Nai Mandi, District Muzaffar Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. Counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case.

As per the allegations in the first information report, two persons robbed the bag of the Doly vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106819011/
1 informant containing Rs. 3,00,000/-, PAN Card, Aadhar Card, original Driving Licence and other papers.

During the course of investigation, husband of the applicant and two others were arrested in Case Crime No. 0590 of 2024, lodged at Police Station Kotwali, District Lalitpur, under Sections 309(4), 318, 336, 338, 248, 217(a), 111, 3(5) and 109 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 3, 25 of the Arms Act.
The aforesaid persons confessed that they had committed the alleged offence.
Further, during the course of investigation, the informant and his wife stated that at the time of withdrawal of the alleged amount from the bank, a lady was also seen in the bank.
On the basis of said statement, the applicant was arrested and implicated.
It is contended that the subsequent statements of the informant and his wife are an afterthought and are unreliable.
There is no substantive evidence to link the applicant with the offence.
False recovery of Rs. 1,30,000/- as well as other articles has been shown from the applicant.
There is no independent witness to the alleged recovery.
The applicant has no criminal history to her credit and averment in this regard has been mentioned in paragraph No. 9 to the affidavit filed in support of the bail application.
The applicant is in jail since 14.07.2024 and in case she is enlarged on bail, she will not misuse the said liberty.
5. Learned AGA has opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.
6. Having heard counsel for the parties and having perused the record, this Court prima facie finds that the applicant was not named in the FIR.
There is no independent witness to the alleged recovery.
There is no substantive evidence to link the applicant with the offence.

The applicant has remained confined for almost four months and after submission of the charge-sheet, there is no hope of early conclusion of trial, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either tamper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness, without commenting on the merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.

7. Let the applicantDoly, involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the conditions that she:
(i) shall appear on the date fixed by the trial court;
(ii) shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence; and,
(iii) shall not pressurize the prosecution witnesses.
8.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Order Date :- 12.11.2024 Kashifa  Doly vs State Of U.P. on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106819011/
